summary: Training deck on plate acceptance for the primary potency assay: control wells, drift checks, accept-or-rerun decisions and how the outcome is recorded before any screen gate conclusion. Speaker notes carry the presenter's reminders and two open reviewer queries.

properties.title: Plate acceptance training (v2)
properties.subject: Primary potency plate acceptance and rerun decisions
properties.keywords: plate acceptance; primary potency; control drift; rerun

slides.title: Plate acceptance for primary potency screens
slides.subtitle: Brindlewythe Biosciences Ltd | Biology training, v2
slides.notes: Second version after the September review. v1 is in the Training folder; use this one for the new starters.

slides.title: Why plate acceptance comes first
bullets: A plate is accepted before any compound on it is read for potency
Accepting a plate means the controls behaved as the protocol expects

bullets.text: Acceptance is recorded on the run sheet, not in the bench notebook

bullets: A failed plate is rerun or excluded; it is never averaged into the set

slides.title: Controls on every plate
bullets: Positive control: reference kinase inhibitor at full response, duplicate wells across the plate
Negative control: vehicle only, same DMSO as the test wells

bullets.text: Keep the DMSO percentage identical across the plate

bullets: Reference compound run as a dose response on each plate

bullets.text: Staurosporine is the house reference for this assay

slides.notes: AV: is the reference titration still on every plate or only on the first plate of a set? Check before the next round.

slides.title: Control drift across a screening set
bullets: Plot the positive and negative control signal against plate order
A slow drift across the set is a reagent or temperature question

bullets.text: Look at the incubator log before reading the compounds

bullets: A step change between two plates usually means a new reagent lot

bullets.text: Record the test lot number on the run sheet

bullets: Drift alone does not fail a plate if both controls still sit inside the window
slides.notes: MS: the drift chart template is on the shared drive under Biology. The old copy in my folder is out of date.

slides.title: Accept or rerun
bullets: Accept when both controls are inside the window
Accept when the reference dose response falls on its curve
Accept with a note when one duplicate well is flagged and the rest agree
bullets_right: Rerun when a control is outside the window
Rerun when the edge wells are the only failures and the reference is off
Escalate to the study director after a second failure on the same test lot

rows: Inside the window across all duplicates
On its curve, same potency range as the last set
Rerun; tell the assay quality coordinator
Hold the set; check the lot record

slides.title: Rerun rules
bullets: One rerun per plate with the same compound plate
A second failure goes to the study director with the run sheet attached

bullets.text: Do not mix a rerun plate into the original set without a note

bullets: Excluded plates stay on the record with the reason
slides.notes: Still unclear whether the one-rerun rule applies to the hepatocyte plates. Ask Anika before the course.

slides.title: Reporting the screen gate
bullets: Acceptance is reported before the potency data
The screen gate decision is separate from any mechanism

bullets.text: Say which plates were rerun and why

bullets: Potency figures go in the biology memo, not on the plate slide

slides.title: Open points for the next revision
bullets: Confirm the drift check frequency with the assay quality coordinator
Add the reagent lot field to the run sheet template
Decide who signs acceptance when the study director is away
slides.notes: Not for circulation. Mostly for me and Ines before the next round.
